title: The Smartest Way to Test Field Marketing Without the Overhead
content:
###  **Testing Should Not Require a Full Commitment** 

Most companies assume that testing whether field marketing works for their business means building a team first — hiring, training, and hoping it pays off. That is backwards. 

###  **The Smarter Sequence** 

Test first, with minimal commitment. See real results. Then decide whether to continue, and in what form — whether that means continuing with a structured pilot or building something in-house with real data in hand. 

###  **Why This Order Matters Financially** 

Building a team first and testing second means absorbing the highest costs — hiring, training, turnover — before knowing if the underlying approach even works for your trade and territory. 

###  **The Low-Overhead Starting Point** 

A short pilot removes the overhead entirely from the testing phase, so the only thing being evaluated is whether the results are there.
